title: XYLayoutLM: Towards Layout-Aware Multimodal Networks For Visually-Rich Document Understanding
abstract: A layout-aware multimodal document model that explicitly addresses reading order and two-dimensional page structure in visually rich documents. Its treatment of ordered layout elements is relevant to preserving semantic document structure for later grounding.

admission.reason: The paper is relevant to document layout and reading order, but its abstract does not add a capability needed strongly enough in this round beyond the more targeted global reading-order relation modeling candidate. It does not address cross-version lineage, grounding, workbook provenance, or the joint robustness gaps.

title: Temporal queries and version management in XML-based document archives
abstract: Studies storage and querying of multi-version XML document histories, including queries over document content and its evolution. It provides transfer evidence for version-aware element histories but does not cover spatial document regions or multimodal attachments.

admission.reason: The topic vocabulary matches version management, but the abstract emphasizes storage and temporal querying over XML histories rather than stable cross-version element correspondence, semantic change mapping, or fine-grained lineage. Stronger XML candidates in this gate address those capabilities more directly. Identity is also UNCHECKED.

title: DocAttriBench: Benchmarking Answer Grounding in Document Visual Question Answering
abstract: Benchmarks document VQA answer attribution at the level of document elements, including text blocks, tables, and images. It evaluates both answer correctness and whether the predicted answer is grounded in the correct supporting element.

admission.reason: Its element-level answer-grounding benchmark is highly relevant, but the capability substantially overlaps the VERIFIED CiteVQA candidate, which already evaluates answer correctness together with localized element-level evidence. With identity UNCHECKED and no distinct cross-version or hierarchical-provenance capability stated in the abstract, it does not justify an additional reading slot.

title: A Prototype Document Image Analysis System for Technical Journals
abstract: An early document-image analysis system that combines page segmentation and structural parsing for technical journal pages. It demonstrates that preservation of page organization and document structure was an explicit document-analysis problem well before modern multimodal models.

admission.reason: The abstract shows page segmentation and structural parsing, but this is foundational layout-analysis evidence rather than a distinctive contribution to the unresolved version-lineage, grounding, provenance, spreadsheet, or joint-robustness gaps. More targeted modern layout and table candidates are available. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Towards Self-Explainable Document Visual Question Answering with Chain-of-Explanation Predictions
abstract: Introduces document VQA reasoning that explicitly identifies relevant evidence and localizes an answer region before producing the answer. The approach is pertinent to making document answers auditable at source-region level.

admission.reason: Localizing relevant evidence and an answer region is on-topic for F6, but that capability is already represented more directly by the admitted CiteVQA benchmark and HierDoc's hierarchical page-to-region routing. The abstract does not add cross-version lineage or a stronger provenance hierarchy.

title: Detecting Changes in XML Documents
abstract: Presents an XML differencing algorithm that matches nodes between old and new document versions and detects operations including subtree moves. Persistent identifiers and structural matching make it relevant to element correspondence across revisions, although the domain is structured XML rather than multimodal attachments.

admission.reason: Matching nodes across XML versions and detecting moves is relevant transfer evidence, but direct cross-version element alignment is already present in the existing corpus and this candidate does not add the stronger persistent-identity or higher-level semantic-change contribution supplied by other XML candidates in this gate. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: BoundingDocs: a Unified Dataset for Document Question Answering with Spatial Annotations
abstract: Associates document question-answer pairs with bounding boxes indicating the exact position of relevant source content. The spatial annotations make it useful for evaluating region-level provenance, while version lineage and workbook cells remain outside its scope.

admission.reason: Bounding-box annotations for document QA are relevant to F6, but the evidence capability is substantially covered by the admitted CiteVQA candidate, which explicitly benchmarks answer attribution with element-level bounding-box citations. This candidate does not extend into version lineage, workbook cells, or a fuller provenance hierarchy.

title: ARIAL: An Agentic Framework for Document VQA with Precise Answer Localization
abstract: Combines document question answering with explicit spatial answer localization through text-to-region alignment. It evaluates both textual answers and localization, directly addressing the need to preserve precise source coordinates alongside an answer.

admission.reason: Precise answer localization is directly relevant to F6, but the abstract describes essentially the same answer-plus-region capability already covered by stronger admitted document-attribution and hierarchical-routing candidates. It does not materially extend the corpus toward cross-version lineage or end-to-end version-page-element-region-span provenance.

title: InstructExcel: A Benchmark for Natural Language Instruction in Excel
abstract: Benchmarks natural-language-driven Excel editing over a broad set of spreadsheet operations and real spreadsheet files. It provides evidence for workbook manipulation capabilities, but it is not a provenance or cross-version cell-lineage benchmark.

admission.reason: The benchmark demonstrates natural-language-driven Excel editing over real spreadsheets, but the abstract does not establish the workbook semantics required by gap-3: formula dependency, hidden content, named ranges, merged-region semantics, cross-sheet provenance, or revised-workbook lineage. Spreadsheet topic overlap alone is insufficient.

title: Challenges in Information-Seeking QA: Unanswerable Questions and Paragraph Retrieval
abstract: Transfer-domain question-answering work that analyzes unanswerable questions together with evidence retrieval. It is relevant to distinguishing genuine evidence absence from successful evidence discovery, although it does not address multimodal document parsing failures or spatial provenance.

admission.reason: The work is transferable to unanswerable QA and evidence retrieval, but the project context already states that the corpus contains unanswerable-question evaluation. The abstract does not distinguish document-specific parser, OCR, layout, localization, and grounding failures, so it does not close the missing engineering contract in gap-5.

title: Change Detection In XML Documents
abstract: Uses top-down and bottom-up XML matching to identify insertions, deletions, updates, copies, and moves between document versions. The operation-level correspondence is useful precedent for revision lineage, while not addressing page regions or multimodal content directly.
venue: International Workshop on XML-Based Data Management

admission.reason: Insertion, deletion, update, copy, and move detection across XML versions is relevant to revision differencing, but this operation-level capability overlaps the existing direct cross-version alignment evidence and the stronger persistent-identity and semantic-change XML candidates selected here. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: High Performance Document Layout Analysis
abstract: Develops robust geometric and statistical methods for document page layout analysis. It is foundational evidence for segmenting heterogeneous pages into meaningful regions before reading-order reconstruction or region-level evidence grounding.
venue: Symposium on Document Image Understanding Technology

admission.reason: The paper is relevant foundational layout-analysis work, but the abstract only establishes page segmentation through geometric and statistical methods. It does not add a distinctive capability beyond stronger candidates for reading-order relations and heterogeneous table topology, and it does not address the unresolved provenance or grounding gaps. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Tracing the lineage of view data in a warehousing environment
abstract: Defines lineage for derived warehouse data and develops methods for tracing an output item back to the source items that contributed to it. The fine-grained source-to-result relationship is transferable to evidence provenance but does not itself model document regions or versions.

admission.reason: Tracing a derived warehouse item back to contributing source items is relevant provenance transfer, but it is generic data lineage and does not add version mapping, spatial hierarchy, or document-region identity. The admitted why/where provenance candidate provides a more directly useful distinction for exact source attribution. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Spatially Grounded Explanations in Vision Language Models for Document Visual Question Answering
abstract: Grounds explanatory rationales for document VQA in spatial subregions of the source document and constrains answering to selected evidence areas. It directly connects language reasoning with localized page evidence.

admission.reason: Spatially grounding explanatory rationales is directly relevant to document VQA, but the abstract does not provide a capability materially different from the admitted answer-attribution and page-to-region evidence-routing papers. It does not extend into cross-version lineage or a complete hierarchical provenance representation.

title: The Open Provenance Model core specification (v1.1)
abstract: Defines a graph-based provenance representation intended to exchange causal histories across systems. Its entity and process relationships are a transferable substrate for hierarchical version lineage, but spatial document coordinates are outside its scope.

admission.reason: The graph-based provenance model is broadly relevant to lineage, but the abstract remains at a generic causal-history exchange level and does not establish hierarchical document source identifiers, version-relative locations, or source-to-answer localization. More specific lineage and source-attribution candidates provide greater value for this round. Identity is UNCHECKED.
